speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry can provide an update on investigations into the recent termination of multiple employees of Surbana Jurong.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) what constitutes due and fair process in terminating employees due to poor performance; (b) what recourse do employees have to access crucial evidence on performance held by employers to prove unfair dismissal; and (c) what are the penalties for employers who disguise retrenchment as termination due to poor performance.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The criteria should be made known to all employees.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Employers should also keep records of their employees' performance and a decision to terminate the service of an employee should be based on documented poor performance.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Where it involves a unionised employee, the union should also be consulted.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If the employee files an appeal of unfair dismissal to MOM, we will first mediate.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Should mediation fail, we will conduct an inquiry and require the employer to show cause and produce evidence to justify the termination.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This remedy is provided under the Employment Act, as well as the Industrial Relations Act for union members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If the employer does not comply with the order, he can be prosecuted.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This episode serves as a good reminder to employers that termination exercises should be conducted in a responsible and sensitive manner.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Big companies have a certain footprint, especially those which are linked to the Government or doing significant business with the public sector.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: How can we strengthen human resource best practices in such companies and are there lessons which can be applied more broadly from what happened in Surbana?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As far as MOM is concerned, we expect all companies to behave in a responsible manner, especially the major employers, whether it is a GLC, MNC, large local enterprise or, for that matter, public services.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM does expect all companies, but especially major employers, to conduct their HR practices in a responsible and progressive manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In this particular case, we are certainly concerned that a major employer could commit such an HR practice lapse.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Looking forward, TAFEP is stepping up efforts to engage the employers out there, including the major ones.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Members may be pleased to know that, last year, I talked about our plan to set up a programme known as the "Human Capital Partnership Programme", which is to reach out to employers, especially the major ones, to work together to value our precious human resources in a more responsive, sensitive, constructive manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That programme will be launched quite soon, within the next few weeks.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would hope that, in time to come, we can continue to reach out to more employers, especially the larger employers, so that mistakes such as this need not happen again in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the case of Surbana, was documented evidence given to the employees of their poor performance?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And do the employees have recourse to ask the employers for evidence, if they are not given the evidence?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Are the employers obliged to give the evidence?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, does MOM step in when it comes to this kind of mass terminations where you have large numbers of people being laid off due to poor performance?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Do they come in to investigate even if there are no reports of unfair dismissal by the employees?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As long as an employee feels that he has been dismissed unfairly, he can just come to MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, he does not need the cooperation of the employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Just come to MOM and we will require the employer to produce the documented proof, failing which we will rule it as an unfair dismissal.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM will come in only when either the union brings it to our attention or the affected employees come to MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This has been the approach because it is not possible for MOM to investigate whenever there is a termination exercise, big or small.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A question for the Minister: would MOM consider having tripartite guidelines for mass terminations, similar to those that we have for mass retrenchments?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners have been and will continue to issue various HR guidelines for progressive HR practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The tripartite partners are also in the process right now of formulating something beyond guidelines.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Hopefully, come the time for the Committee of Supply (COS) debate, I will be able to share with this House on how we can strengthen progressive HR practices in our HR community.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With this label, it is very difficult for them or it would be an additional challenge for them to find the next job.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I spent many years with the Labour Movement and now with MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If the performance of the employees is not up to the mark, there could be contributing factors on the part of the employers as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, performance management should be a joint responsibility of employees and employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In most organisations, if it reaches such a stage whereby the employees and employers can no longer continue the working relationship, they will find a way to go separate ways, but you do not label the person publicly.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I hope that we will not come across another case where a company does a major termination and labels the employees as poor performers publicly.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the end of the day, yes, it may be poor performance in one organisation, but it does not mean a person cannot do well in other places.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I had mentioned, the work environment, HR practices and so on are also contributing factors.
